Main.sentence: Stanley Armour Dunham (March 23, 1918 – February 8, 1992) was an American furniture salesman and the maternal grandfather of ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ , the 44th ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ .
He and his wife ___E:Madelyn Payne Dunham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madelyn_Dunham)___ raised Obama from the age of 10 in ___E:Honolulu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu)___ , Hawaii.
Stanley Armour Dunham was born in ___E:Wichita, Kansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita,_Kansas)___ , the younger of two sons to Ralph Waldo Emerson Dunham, Sr. and Ruth Lucille Armour.
His father's ancestors settled in ___E:Kempton, Indiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kempton,_Indiana)___ , in the 1840s, before relocating to Kansas.

His parents were married on October 3, 1915, at a home on South Saint Francis St. in Wichita, and opened The Travelers' Cafe on William Street situated between the old firehouse and the old Wichita City Hotel.
On November 25, 1926, at age 8, Dunham discovered his mother's body after she had committed suicide.

Subsequently, Dunham's father placed him and his older brother Ralph Waldo Emerson Dunham, Jr. in the care of their maternal grandparents in ___E:El Dorado, Kansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Dorado,_Kansas)___ .

A rebellious teenager, Dunham allegedly punched his high school principal and spent some time drifting, hopping rail cars to ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ , then ___E:California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California)___ , and back again.
He married ___E:Madelyn Lee Payne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madelyn_Dunham)___ on May 5, 1940, the night of her ___E:senior prom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prom)___ .

Dunham enlisted as a private in the ___E:U.S. Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Army)___ on January 18, 1942, at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, and served in the ___E:European Theatre of World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Theatre_of_World_War_II)___ with the 1830th Ordnance Supply and Maintenance Company, Aviation.
During D-Day, this unit helped to support the ___E:Ninth Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninth_Air_Force)___ .

Dunham and his brother were deployed to France six weeks after D-Day. Before the ___E:Invasion of Normandy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Normandy)___ , the brothers once met accidentally as Stanley Dunham went in search of rations at a hotel in London, where his brother Ralph Dunham happened to be staying.

Madelyn Dunham gave birth to their daughter ___E:Stanley Ann Dunham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Ann_Dunham)___ , who was later known as Ann, at St. Francis Hospital in Wichita on November 29, 1942. During the war, Madelyn Dunham worked on a ___E:Boeing B-29 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_B-29)___ assembly line in Wichita.
After two years of military service in Europe (1943–1945), Dunham was discharged from the U.S.

Army on August 30, 1945. After the war, the family moved to ___E:Berkeley, California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berkeley,_California)___ , so he could pursue study at the ___E:University of California, Berkeley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley)___ and then eventually back to El Dorado, Kansas, where Dunham managed a furniture store.

In 1955, after the Dunhams moved to ___E:Seattle, Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle,_Washington)___ , Dunham worked as a salesman for the Standard-Grunbaum Furniture Company, and his daughter Ann attended middle school.
The family lived in an apartment in the Wedgwood Estates in the ___E:Wedgwood, Seattle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wedgwood,_Seattle)___ neighborhood.
In 1956 they moved to the Shorewood Apartments on ___E:Mercer Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercer_Island)___ , a Seattle suburb.
Ann attended high school there, and they stayed until she graduated in 1960. In 1957, Dunham started working for the Doces Majestic Furniture Company.
The family then moved to ___E:Honolulu, Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu,_Hawaii)___ , where Dunham found a better furniture store opportunity.
Madelyn Dunham started working at the Bank of Hawaii in 1960, and was promoted as one of the bank's first female vice presidents in 1970.

In ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ 's memoir, Dreams From My Father , he wrote, "One of my earliest memories is of sitting on my grandfather's shoulders as the astronauts from one of the Apollo missions arrived at Hickam Air Force Base after a successful splashdown".

At 10 years old, Barack Obama moved in with the Dunhams in Honolulu to attend school in the U.S. while his mother and stepfather ___E:Lolo Soetoro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lolo_Soetoro)___ were living in ___E:Jakarta, Indonesia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakarta,_Indonesia)___ .
His mother later came back to Hawaii to pursue graduate studies, but when she returned to Indonesia in 1977 for her master's fieldwork, Obama stayed in the United States with his grandparents.
Obama wrote in his memoir, Dreams From My Father , "I'd arrived at an unspoken pact with my grandparents: I could live with them and they'd leave me alone so long as I kept my trouble out of sight".

Dunham died in ___E:Honolulu, Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu,_Hawaii)___ , on February 8, 1992, and is interred in the ___E:Punchbowl National Cemetery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punchbowl_National_Cemetery)___ .

Dunham is a direct descendant of ___E:Jonathan Singletary Dunham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Singletary_Dunham)___ , a prominent early American settler who left the ___E:Plymouth Colony U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth_Colony)___ to build the first ___E:gristmill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gristmill)___ in ___E:New Jersey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey)___ .

The most recent native White European ancestor was Falmouth Kearney, a farmer who emigrated from ___E:Moneygall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moneygall)___ , ___E:County Offaly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Offaly)___ , Ireland, during the ___E:Great Irish Famine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Famine_(Ireland))___ and settled in ___E:Jefferson Township, Tipton County, Indiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Township,_Tipton_County,_Indiana)___ , United States.
Kearney's youngest daughter, Mary Ann (Kearney) Dunham, was Stanley Dunham's paternal grandmother.

In addition to his grandson Barack Obama, Stanley Dunham's distant relatives include six U.S. presidents: ___E:James Madison U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Madison)___ , ___E:Harry Truman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Truman)___ , ___E:Lyndon Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_Johnson)___ , ___E:Jimmy Carter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter)___ , ___E:George H. W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush)___ and ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ .
Dunham and ___E:Wild Bill Hickok U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_Bill_Hickok)___ are sixth cousins, four times removed, through Jacob Dunham.
